**Generating Captions for the Storm Video**

Okay, so I've been tasked with crafting 60 individual captions, each a second long, for this video starting at 3:30. That puts the final caption at 4:30. I've dissected the video into these one-second intervals and made brief notes on what's visible in each to create captions.

It starts with a moody, pre-storm shot of a road and some telephone poles under a dark, greenish sky. Then we get inside a vehicle, likely a dashcam, as the storm hits - heavy rain, wind, and a stopped car at a dirt road.  I see a prominent storm cloud in the sky that builds in intensity.

The next few intervals focus on the fury of the storm from within the vehicle. Then there's a shift back to an external shot where I catch sight of a funnel cloud forming, initially faint, but growing more defined in the dark, green-tinged sky. It retracts a bit, dissipating back into the cloud base. The storm structure is quite impressive.

After the funnel cloud fades, we get wide shots of the supercell, showcasing its immense scale and ominous presence, stretching across the horizon.

Then we go back to the dashcam again, now in motion, passing industrial-looking white tanks, fields, and hay bales. A new funnel cloud, a tornado, emerges in the distance, becoming more defined. The vehicle seems to be chasing the storm or at least observing it. There are parked cars off to the side, also watching.

The vehicle continues driving, offering a clear view of the tornado touching down in the fields, with the storm still in its full glory. We get views of industrial buildings in the foreground against the vast storm cloud. The final moments maintain this perspective, encapsulating a remarkable scene. I have all the key features for each caption. Now, the format: I'll need to turn all this into a JSON array, with start and end times, and these short captions.
